Headless Engine API: build scenes and render images without the editor

Stable Engine Last updated: 2026-11-18

Automate the engine through the C ABI: build scenes, add components, write materials, generate terrain and water, and render RGBA images offscreen with no window.

Everything Doppio does to the engine goes through one C ABI, libcaffeine-capi (include/caffeine/capi/EngineAPI.h, CAFFEINE_CAPI_VERSION 8). Anything the editor can do, a script can do: create entities, add components, write materials, generate terrain and water, move the camera and render the scene to RGBA pixels, offscreen, with no window. This page is for automating that: test scenes, generated images, thumbnails, regression pictures, batch renders.

The shape of the API#

Idea What it means
Session caffeine_session_create() makes one scene (its own ECS world). Everything else takes the session. Destroy it with caffeine_session_destroy.
Entities uint32_t ids. caffeine_session_create_entity(session, name) returns CAFFEINE_ENTITY_NONE on failure. Transforms are position, rotation (Euler degrees) and scale. Parent with caffeine_session_set_entity_parent.
Components by name Components are described at run time. List them with caffeine_component_type_count/at, their fields with caffeine_component_type_field_at, add one with caffeine_session_add_component(session, entity, type_id) and set a field with caffeine_session_entity_component_field_set. Field kinds: f32, bool, i32, u32, vec2/3/4, string, enum (by option index), colour. This is the same reflection the editor Inspector uses, so a new component shows up here without an API change.
Assets caffeine_session_set_asset_root(session, folder) sets the project folder. Asset paths in components are relative to it (nature/materials/oak.mat). caffeine_session_asset_project_path and caffeine_session_resolve_path convert between forms.
Materials .mat files. caffeine_material_default/load/save edit them; caffeine_session_apply_material(session, entity, path) assigns one. A material is an asset, never part of a mesh.
Results Every call returns CaffeineResult: OK, ERROR, INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND. Check it.
Version caffeine_capi_version() tells you what the library you loaded supports. Terrain needs 8, water 7.

Render an image (the whole loop)#

text
create session -> set asset root -> create entities + components -> assign materials
-> set camera -> (optional) viewport settings -> render -> write PNG

caffeine_session_render(session, width, height, pixels, pixel_bytes) fills width * height * 4 bytes of RGBA8 and blocks until done. For interactive use, caffeine_session_render_begin then caffeine_session_render_poll until CAFFEINE_RENDER_READY does not block. Call caffeine_session_tick(session, dt) between renders when something animates (water, particles).

The camera is an orbit camera (CaffeineCamera): yaw and pitch in radians, distance in metres, focus the point it looks at. CaffeineViewportSettings has show_grid (on by default: turn it off for a clean picture), anti_aliasing (0 off, 1 FXAA, 2 TAA) and render_scale (0.5 to 2.0, supersampling).

Runnable example (Rust)#

doppio/crates/engine/examples/render_scene.rs builds a ground plane, a cube, a sphere and a sun, writes three .mat files, assigns them, aims the camera and saves a PNG:

bash
cmake --build build --target caffeine-capi -j
cd doppio
cargo run -p doppio-engine --example render_scene -- /tmp/scene.png

The doppio-engine crate is a thin safe wrapper over the C functions (create_entity, add_component, set_component_field, apply_material, set_camera, render...); it is the only Rust crate that loads the library, and CAFFEINE_CAPI_LIB overrides where it looks.

From Python (no build step)#

python
import ctypes as C
lib = C.CDLL("build/libcaffeine-capi.so")          # .dylib / .dll elsewhere
lib.caffeine_session_create.restype = C.c_void_p
lib.caffeine_session_create_entity.restype = C.c_uint32
lib.caffeine_session_create_entity.argtypes = [C.c_void_p, C.c_char_p]
lib.caffeine_session_render.argtypes = [C.c_void_p, C.c_uint32, C.c_uint32, C.c_void_p, C.c_size_t]

session = lib.caffeine_session_create()
lib.caffeine_session_create_entity(session, b"Thing")
w, h = 640, 360
pixels = (C.c_uint8 * (w * h * 4))()
assert lib.caffeine_session_render(session, w, h, pixels, len(pixels)) == 0
# bytes(pixels) is RGBA8; hand it to Pillow / numpy / imageio

Any language with a C FFI works the same way: declare the functions you use, pass plain structs.

Generate content, then render it#

  • Terrain. caffeine_session_set_terrain(session, entity, &CaffeineTerrain, heights, splat_rgba) takes a normalised height grid (0..1, row-major) and optional splat weights (ground, rock, dirt, mud). The four layers are the terrain component's Splat Layer Paths 1..4 string fields: set them to project textures (the Terrain Generator writes terrain/layers/<layer>.png plus a .mat per layer and sets the paths from each material's albedo map). caffeine_session_terrain_height samples it.
  • Water. caffeine_session_set_water(session, entity, &water) makes an animated surface; assign a .mat to the entity and the water is drawn with it. caffeine_session_water_height samples the surface at a time, so tick before you sample.
  • Nature and meshes. Write .obj files into the project and set a Mesh Filter to Custom with the Mesh path (this is what Place in scene does for trees and rocks).
  • Scenes. caffeine_session_save_scene / load_scene read and write .caf, so a generated scene can be reopened in Doppio or loaded by the runtime. snapshot / restore give cheap undo points.

Textures and material previews without a scene#

caffeine_texture_generate_map, caffeine_texture_pack_maps (ORM and engine packings), caffeine_texture_save_rgba/rgba16 and caffeine_texture_load_rgba work on pictures directly. caffeine_session_render_material_preview(_ex) renders a lit sphere, cube or plane for a .mat without building a scene, which is how thumbnails and the material gallery (scripts/render-material-gallery.sh) are made.

Practical notes#

  • Rendering uses an SDL GPU device and draws offscreen: the render calls open no window. It was checked on a Linux desktop with a GPU; a machine with no GPU at all is untested.
  • Use one session from one thread at a time; the API makes no promise of concurrent access to a session.
  • For regression pictures compare with a tolerance: results can differ slightly between GPUs and drivers.
  • Assets are referenced by path: set the asset root first, and prefer relative paths so a scene moves with its project.
  • The generators in Doppio only call this API, so anything they place can be reproduced from a script.
